plants.name: Prunus mume
plants.description: A small deciduous tree that produces fragrant five-petaled blossoms on bare branches in late winter, before its leaves emerge. It is widely cultivated in ume groves and gardens and is a classic subject of East Asian art and poetry.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late winter to early spring (January to March)
plants.location: Japan, China, Korea; cultivated in temperate gardens worldwide
plants.funFact: Ume blossoms often open while snow is still on the ground, so they symbolize perseverance and hope. The fruit is pickled to make umeboshi and used in plum wine.

plants.name: Galanthus nivalis
plants.description: A small bulbous perennial with nodding, bell-shaped white flowers marked with green on the inner petals. It carpets woodlands and gardens, often pushing up through frost and snow.
plants.location: Europe, naturalized in the UK and North America
plants.funFact: Snowdrops contain galantamine, a compound that has been developed into a medication used to treat symptoms of Alzheimer's disease.

plants.name: Protea cynaroides
plants.description: A dramatic evergreen shrub of the fynbos with huge flower heads made of showy bracts surrounding a central cluster of tiny flowers. Its blooming peaks in the southern hemisphere's late summer into autumn, so it is often seen in flower around this date.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late summer to autumn in the southern hemisphere (peak February to May, with some blooms in spring)
plants.funFact: The king protea is South Africa's national flower, and its flower heads can reach over 30 cm across. It is adapted to fire and resprouts after bushfires.

plants.name: Acacia pycnantha
plants.description: A fast-growing Australian tree or large shrub covered in fluffy, fragrant golden ball-shaped flower clusters. Although it peaks in late winter and spring, some wattles and other acacias are in bloom across Australia in late February in cooler, higher or southern regions.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late winter to spring (July to October), with some wattle species flowering in other months
plants.funFact: Golden wattle is Australia's national floral emblem, and National Wattle Day is celebrated on September 1.
